pages.title: Motorcycle Oil Grades Explained
pages.summary: Understanding SAE viscosity ratings, JASO MA/MA2, and API classifications.
pages.content:
SAE Viscosity

The first number (e.g. 10W-40) indicates cold-start viscosity. The W means Winter. Lower numbers flow better in cold conditions.

The second number (e.g. 10W-40) indicates viscosity at operating temperature. Higher numbers provide thicker protection at high heat.

JASO Certification

  • JASO MA — Standard for wet-clutch motorcycles. No friction modifiers that cause clutch slip.
  • JASO MA2 — Higher friction performance for modern bikes. Preferred for most current motorcycles.
  • JASO MB — For scooters with CVT. Not suitable for manual-clutch bikes.

API Rating

Look for API SG or higher. Avoid automotive oils with energy-conserving labels — they contain friction modifiers harmful to wet clutches.

pages.title: Contributing to MotoX Wiki
pages.summary: How to add or update motorcycle specifications.
pages.content:
How to Contribute

MotoX Wiki is community-maintained. You can contribute by:

  1. Forking the repository on GitHub
  2. Editing data/motorcycles.json, data/pages.json, or data/settings.json
  3. Running npm run build:data to regenerate indexes and detail files
  4. Committing changes and opening a pull request

Data Guidelines

  • Always include a reference (service manual, OEM documentation, manufacturer spec sheet)
  • Include year ranges and market/region when specs vary
  • Use standard units (Nm for torque, L for volume, hp/kW for power) with conversions in parentheses
  • Put general specs in sections.general_specs and service figures in sections.service
  • Leave a field out rather than filling it with a generic value — an empty field is better than wrong data
  • Mark unverified data in the notes field or a custom section

pages.title: Metric Fastener Torque Guide
pages.summary: Typical dry torque values for common metric bolts and nuts by property class.
pages.content:
Typical dry torque values

Use these values only as a general reference for clean, dry, lightly oiled or plated threads where the manufacturer does not specify a torque. Always prefer the torque figure in the official workshop manual, especially for engine, brake, suspension and safety-critical fasteners.

Thread8.810.912.9
M55.5 Nm8 Nm9.5 Nm
M69.5 Nm14 Nm16.5 Nm
M823 Nm34 Nm40 Nm
M1046 Nm68 Nm80 Nm
M1280 Nm117 Nm140 Nm
M14128 Nm187 Nm225 Nm
M16197 Nm290 Nm345 Nm

Notes

  • These are approximate dry-thread values for metric coarse threads. Lubricated threads can require 20–30% less torque for the same clamp load.
  • Reduce torque for aluminium threads, hollow fasteners, banjo bolts and fasteners into plastic.
  • Use a calibrated torque wrench and tighten in stages where a sequence is specified.
  • Never reuse torque-to-yield or single-use fasteners.
